record.what_it_does: Intercom is a customer messaging and support platform providing a REST API to manage contacts, conversations, tickets, articles, and AI (Fin) content for building support/helpdesk integrations.
record.auth_notes: Access Tokens (a static Bearer token issued per-app in the Developer Hub) are for private apps accessing your own workspace's data. OAuth2 is required for public apps that access other people's Intercom workspaces — Intercom's terms prohibit asking users for their Access Token instead of implementing OAuth. Both methods are used as an 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' header.
record.access_notes: Developers can create a free development workspace and an app in the Developer Hub to get a working Access Token or set up OAuth immediately, at no cost. Development workspaces have limitations (US-only, max 20 users/leads, no outbound email) and cannot be converted to production; real customer data requires a paid Intercom workspace, but API credentials for building/testing are free and self-serve.

evidence.quote: An Access Token is for if you're using the API to access data in your own Intercom workspace
OAuth is for if you're building a public app that accesses other people's Intercom data
Development workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only.
Intercom hosts a remote MCP server that follows the authenticated remote MCP specification
The Intercom MCP Server provides 14 tools for interacting with the Intercom API

record.open_questions: Whether distributing an unlisted OAuth app to external customers (without App Store review) is unrestricted, versus requiring Intercom review for public App Store listing, was not fully confirmed from a fetched page.
